title: Casa Trencadís
brief: An explorable three.js interior built entirely in the register of the visionary organic architect — one warm salon, roughly 9 × 7 m, where every element speaks Gaudí's grammar. A colonnade of real catenary arches (y = a·cosh(x/a), the curve that carries its own load, inverted) marches down the arch hall; the plaster walls undulate like drawn breath via sine-displaced geometry; the ceiling is a shallow ribbed vault with a glazed oculus and a soft shaft of light; a twisting organic column and a floor medallion are sheathed head-to-foot in procedural trencís (broken-tile mosaic in teal, gold and rose set into dark grout); the whole south wall gives way to one great lobed organic window with leaded wrought-iron muntins and coloured glass roundels, pouring honeyed Mediterranean daylight into the room; a cantilevered sandstone stair fans and turns up the east corner laced by an iron balustrade that curls like a tendril. Furnished sparely — a steam-bent oak window bench, a low amoeba-topped organic table on a wool rug, an iron candelabra, mosaic pots with blade leaves. Fully procedural geometry AND materials: every texture (troweled lime plaster, honey sandstone, the trencís shards) is drawn on a canvas at runtime, no external assets. Warm soft lighting (hemisphere + ambient fill, a warm directional sun through the window, soft PCF shadows), ACES tone mapping, a Day/Dusk swing that lowers the sun and lifts the candelabra glow. Drag to orbit and scroll to zoom (OrbitControls); tap one of four saved viewpoints (Arch Hall, Mosaic Column, Window Seat, Sculpted Stair) to glide the camera on an eased path; or press Walk for first-person WASD movement with pointer-lock mouse-look at eye height, clamped inside the room. Click any feature for a floating callout naming its material and the Gaudí principle at play (catenary structure, nature geometry, trencís, light as material, wrought iron). A collapsible 'About this' exec-summary opens top-left; prefers-reduced-motion disables auto-glide and flicker.
da: Catalan modernism, hand-crafted and warm — honeyed ochre and sandstone surfaces, troweled lime plaster, a trencís mosaic accent in teal (#1F8C82), gold (#D9A536) and rose (#C86B7A) over dark grout, wrought-iron near-black (#241C1B) curves, and a great lobed window pouring Mediterranean daylight; soft realistic sun with PCF shadows and ACES tone mapping, floating amber-glass UI, Marcellus inscriptional titles + Jost interface — organic, curved and mosaic, a deliberately different designer from the plain-plaster warm-apartment walk-through and from every other library piece.
